subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event taxonomy and a new manifest-authorized public plugin emission contract as permanent supported surfaces?
rationale: The answer fixes long-lived plugin API, manifest compatibility, operator trust, session attribution, and security semantics that cannot safely be selected by contributor-side repair automation.

options.title: Sponsor a host-bound contract
options.body: Approve the direction only after the helper is internalized, permissions are parsed and validated, host identity is captured, complete payloads are validated, and installed-plugin proof is added.

options.title: Keep safety emission internal
options.body: Land only maintainer-approved core diagnostic events and omit the public plugin API and manifest permission surface for now.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Leave this PR and its dependent series unmerged until the canonical issue establishes the taxonomy, storage, privacy, and trust model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-bound contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction only after the helper is internalized, permissions are parsed and validated, host identity is captured, complete payloads are validated, and installed-plugin proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin manifest and runtime history makes this person the strongest available owner for deciding whether the new public contract belongs in core.
